discovery: Quantum key distribution: secure communication based on the laws of quantum physics

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the quantum properties of single photons, through no-cloning and measurement disturbance, allow two parties to establish a secret key whose security rests on physical law rather than computational assumptions. With Bennett they also gave the first experimental demonstration (1989–92). Ekert (E91) independently tied key security to entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities, linking the foundations of quantum mechanics directly to a practical task and founding the device-independent approach. These ideas started quantum information science as an experimental discipline. They led to multiphoton entanglement experiments, teleportation, fibre and satellite QKD networks, and today's quantum communication infrastructures. Few contributions have turned questions about the nature of quantum measurement and nonlocality so completely into laboratory reality and technology of lasting value to humankind.
